title: The Laws of Attraction
coreMove: Read attraction as a paced system of repeated contact, reciprocity, calibrated self-disclosure, and supportive responsiveness.
sourcePressure: The ch04 source widens from immediate liking into attraction through repeated contact, reciprocity, self-disclosure, and support. It warns that frequency cannot fix one-sided support or premature intimacy.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Collapsing attraction into romance, frequency, or fast disclosure.

sourceAnchors.name: reciprocal self-disclosure
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch04 sidecar says the move from acquaintanceship to friendship is marked by reciprocal self-disclosure.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Disclosure begins to help only when it travels both ways and the relationship has room to hold it.

sourceAnchors.name: Beverley Fehr
sourceAnchors.detail: The structured ch04 source sidecar lists Beverley Fehr among proper nouns in the support bundle for attraction, reciprocity, and friendship research framing.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The research tradition around friendship is useful here for one plain reason: attraction grows best when contact becomes reciprocal, not merely frequent.

tryThisNow: share one personal fact with someone

exampleSpecs.domain: a disaster-relief volunteer roster where two crews cross paths every morning but do not trust each other
exampleSpecs.audience: a field coordinator reading why repeated contact has stalled
exampleSpecs.stakes: handoffs are slow during flood cleanup
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator adds a reciprocal handoff ritual where each crew states one risk and one need, turning contact into mutual support
exampleSpecs.firstImage: mud drying on laminated shift cards

exampleSpecs.domain: an indie game studio playtest channel with fans who comment often but never feel close to the team
exampleSpecs.audience: a community lead trying to build real attraction to the project
exampleSpecs.stakes: a public beta could lose its core testers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What changes when the lead shares a small design tradeoff and asks testers to share their own play constraints?

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood running group where a newcomer attends every week but remains peripheral
exampleSpecs.audience: a group organizer who confuses attendance with attraction
exampleSpecs.stakes: the runner may stop showing up before the charity race
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes Emily four Saturdays to see that nobody has traded real information with the newcomer beyond pace and route
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a race bib pinned to a cork board

exampleSpecs.domain: a small architecture firm pairing a client and project lead over a home renovation
exampleSpecs.audience: a project lead who needs supportiveness without premature intimacy
exampleSpecs.stakes: the client is anxious about spending savings on a rebuild
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "We had the same fear when we opened the west wall," Nicolas says, then stops before turning the meeting into his story and asks what risk feels largest to the client

exampleSpecs.domain: a parent committee planning a school fundraiser after a tense year
exampleSpecs.audience: a committee chair rebuilding attraction among volunteers
exampleSpecs.stakes: one-sided support will leave three parents carrying everything
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chair shifts from broad gratitude to paired reciprocal commitments, so each parent gives and receives support visibly
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the smell of poster paint in the multipurpose room

exampleSpecs.domain: a freelance photography collective where members trade referrals unevenly
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder diagnosing why the group feels attractive to some and draining to others
exampleSpecs.stakes: unreciprocated leads could break the collective
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 4:45 p.m., Chiara maps who shared leads and who only received them, then resets the group around reciprocal support before the next client call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wall calendar marked with referral arrows

skillTargets: diagnose why repeated contact has not become attraction
identify one-sided support as a warning sign
separate broad human attraction from romance-only framing

tryThisNowSpec: Choose one developing bond and write whether repeated contact, reciprocity, disclosure, or support is doing the most work, then name the weakest piece.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
